official.deadline_note: The 2026/2027 call (no 19/2026 of 30 April 2026) closed on 29 May 2026 at 3:00 PM Warsaw local time, with results announced by NAWA on 3 August 2026, so no current-cycle deadline is published. The programme page and the NAWA news index carry no dated window for a 2027/2028 call.
official.application_cycle: Annual call published each spring for the following academic year; the 2026/2027 cycle was call no 19/2026 of 30 April 2026 and is closed
official.status_note: NAWA's news item for the 2026 call stated that applications had to be submitted electronically via the NAWA ICT system by 29 May 2026, 3:00 PM Warsaw local time; the catalogue's stored record notes results were published on 3 August 2026. No open round is published as at 10 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: NAWA's programme page states: 'the Programme provides an exemption from tuition fees at public universities.' The 2026 call announcement lists 'tuition fee exemption at public universities' among the scholarship components. Exemption applies at public higher education institutions; the programme explicitly covers both public and non-public academic HEIs supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education, so non-public institutions are not covered by the exemption.
benefits: A monthly NAWA scholarship of PLN 2,000
Tuition fee exemption at public universities
A one-off travel allowance for coming to Poland
Scholarship paid during the statutory period of full-time second-cycle studies
eligibility: Foreigner who is a citizen of one of the countries and territories listed in the call (44 listed, including Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Chile, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, Romania, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, Republic of Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom, United States, Uruguay, and residents of Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan)
Obtained a first-cycle (Bachelor's) degree in a Programme country no earlier than 2024, or is a final-year first-cycle student who will obtain the degree by 15 July 2026 (2026 call condition)

Plans to commence full-time second-cycle (Master's) studies in Poland in the 2026/27 academic year at an academic HEI supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that has concluded a framework agreement with NAWA
Has not previously received a NAWA Director's scholarship under NAWA second-cycle degree programmes
Documented proficiency in Polish at minimum B2 level if the chosen programme is conducted in Polish, or in English at minimum B2 level if it is conducted in English
requirements: Choose the university and field of study independently from the offer of universities listed in the call
Apply for admission to the chosen university separately from, and independently of, the NAWA application
Submit the NAWA scholarship application electronically in the NAWA ICT system
Prepare the application in Polish or English
documents: NAWA scholarship application submitted in the NAWA tele-informational system (programs.nawa.gov.pl)
Previous higher education diploma with certified translation, or a model certificate from the university for final-year undergraduate students
Recognised Polish or English language certificate from the current call's accepted list, evidencing at least B2 level in the language of instruction
selection_criteria: Formal eligibility check followed by substantive merit assessment by NAWA
coverage: Monthly NAWA scholarship of PLN 2,000 for the statutory period of full-time second-cycle studies
Tuition fee exemption at public universities
One-off travel allowance for coming to Poland
application_method: Create an account and submit the application electronically via the NAWA ICT system at programs.nawa.gov.pl
Separately apply for admission to the chosen university and meet its admission requirements
official.application_route: Apply online through the NAWA ICT system during the published call, and separately secure university admission yourself - NAWA does not intermediate admission
official.citizenship_residency: Open only to foreigners - citizens of the countries and territories listed in the call; Polish nationals are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is designed exclusively for international candidates from the listed high socio-economic development countries and territories
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The Programme does not provide for a call for applications for fields of study offered by higher education institutions supervised by other ministries; fields must be chosen from HEIs supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that have a framework agreement with NAWA
official.duration: The statutory period of full-time second-cycle (Master's) studies at the chosen Polish academic higher education institution
official.description: The Poland My First Choice NAWA programme encourages young talented people from the listed countries to pursue studies at Polish academic higher education institutions, offering a scholarship during the statutory period of full-time second-cycle studies together with an exemption from tuition fees at public universities. Applicants select the university and field of study independently, and NAWA does not act as an intermediary in admission.
official.program_type: Government scholarship for international master's students
official.english_requirement: Candidates must provide proof of knowledge of the language of instruction of the chosen study programme - Polish or English - at least at B2 level; applications may be submitted in Polish or English

verification.notes: Read NAWA's own programme page and NAWA's 2026 call news item on nawa.gov.pl. The 2026 call states PLN 2,000 per month, tuition fee exemption at public universities and a one-off travel allowance, with a 29 May 2026 15:00 Warsaw deadline - this supersedes the PLN 1,800 figure held in the catalogue. No open round is published.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a Polish government master's scholarship worth PLN 2,000 per month plus tuition exemption at public universities, but only for nationals of the 44 listed high-income countries and territories - if your passport is not on that list the award is closed to you regardless of your grades. The 2026/2027 round shut on 29 May 2026 and results came out on 3 August 2026, so realistically you are preparing for the spring 2027 call; use the gap to secure or plan university admission, because NAWA will not do that part for you. Choose a public university if you want the tuition exemption to have any value, since non-public institutions are inside the scheme's scope but outside the fee exemption.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Graduates of the listed countries who already hold, or can realistically win, a place on a full-time English- or Polish-taught master's at a Polish public university with a NAWA framework agreement
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality appears on the current call's country list before investing any effort - the list is reissued each call
Shortlist Polish public universities that hold a framework agreement with NAWA and open the relevant master's programmes in English or Polish
Book a B2-or-above Polish or English language certificate from the call's recognised list; an unlisted test will not count
Run your university admission application in parallel, since NAWA explicitly does not intermediate admission
Have your bachelor's diploma translated and certified, and start the apostille or legalisation process early if your country needs it
common_rejection_risks: Applying without simultaneously pursuing university admission - NAWA will not admit you and the scholarship assumes you are already admitted
Submitting a language certificate that is not on the current call's recognised list, or one below B2
Picking a programme at an institution supervised by another ministry, which the call explicitly excludes
Assuming the fee exemption covers a non-public university, where tuition remains payable in full
Missing the narrow electronic submission window - the 2026 call closed mid-afternoon Warsaw time on a single date
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation and day-to-day living costs in Poland beyond the PLN 2,000 monthly scholarship, plus tuition at any non-public institution, residence and visa costs, and health insurance arrangements
document_audit: Your degree certificate needs a certified translation; final-year students must supply the university's model certificate instead, so request it well before the deadline

The language certificate must be on the call's own recognised list and must match the language your chosen programme is actually taught in - a Polish certificate is useless for an English-taught programme and vice versa
Proof of nationality is mandatory and must reflect the eligible country as listed in that call
alerts: The stipend is edition-specific: PLN 2,000 was published for the 2026/2027 call, and older secondary sources still quote PLN 1,800 - always take the figure from the current call announcement
NAWA publishes this call in spring with results in early August, so an applicant starting in October of year X is targeting the call published in spring of year X+1 for an autumn start
Countries on the list have varied between editions, so eligibility established in one year is not a guarantee for the next
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Watch NAWA's news page for the spring call announcement, verify your country is listed, submit the electronic application in the NAWA ICT system inside the short published window, and run your university admission application in parallel - both must succeed

official.deadline_note: The 2025 edition required National Commissions of invited Member States to transmit endorsed applications by Monday 26 May 2025, Midnight Paris time, and that edition is now closed. UNESCO publishes no deadline for a subsequent edition on this page, so there is no current-cycle date to record.
official.application_cycle: Annual edition; the 2025 edition placed 28 six-month fellowships running 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026 at the AGH University of Krakow and is closed for applications
official.status_note: UNESCO's page states plainly: 'The 2025 edition of this Programme is closed for applications.' No 2026 or 2027 edition has been announced on the page as at 10 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: UNESCO publishes: 'Free tuition for six (6) months and access to the university facilities based on the local regulations.'
benefits: Free tuition for six months and access to university facilities based on the local regulations
Monthly allowance of 1800 PLN for BSc degree students and 2200 PLN for MSc degree students, intended to cover all living expenses and accommodation in Poland

One-time special allowance of 1800 PLN (BSc) or 2200 PLN (MSc) paid upon arrival in Poland, covering the obligatory arrival medical check-up and cultural, historical or touristic visits, conferences, workshops and seminars related to the studies
International travel expenses by the most direct, economical route from the beneficiary's country to and from Poland, covered by UNESCO
Health insurance taken out and paid for by UNESCO for fellows declared medically fit
One-time special pocket allowance of US$120
eligibility: National of one of the 57 invited Member States listed in Annex II (21 African, 2 Arab States, 22 Asia-Pacific and 12 Latin America and Caribbean states)
Holds a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD degree, submitted as certified copies in English with Apostille or authorised by the competent authority
Meets the field-specific qualifications set out in Annex III for the chosen project - some projects restrict candidates to certain regions
Endorsed and nominated by the National Commission for UNESCO of the candidate's own country - individual applications are not accepted
requirements: Contact the National Commission for UNESCO of your country first to enquire about national-level procedures
Choose a maximum of three of the proposed projects and give a priority number for each
Submit the application to your National Commission early enough for it to transmit the documents to UNESCO Paris by the deadline
Once endorsed, submit the application by e-mail to agh.poland@unesco.org and complete the online information sheet by the stated deadline
documents: UNESCO fellowships application form, all 4 pages, duly completed in English using capital letters
A copy of the applicant's passport
A copy of the identity photo of the applicant

Certified copies in English of the Bachelor's, Master's or PhD degree obtained, with Apostille or authorised by the competent authority (legalisation in the country of issue where Apostille is not recognised)
A UNESCO certificate of language knowledge, duly completed by a relevant authority, if the candidate's mother tongue is not English
Two letters of recommendation from people familiar with the candidate's work, confirming their qualifications
selection_criteria: Only applications endorsed by a National Commission for UNESCO are considered, owing to the intergovernmental character of UNESCO
The selection of fellowship recipients is made and decided by the concerned Polish authorities, taking into consideration gender equality and diversity
Candidatures with incomplete applications, or submitted after the deadline, will not be considered
coverage: Free tuition for six months and access to university facilities
Monthly allowance of 1800 PLN (BSc) or 2200 PLN (MSc) intended to cover all living expenses and accommodation in Poland
One-time special allowance of 1800 PLN (BSc) or 2200 PLN (MSc) on arrival in Poland
International travel to and from Poland by the most direct, economical route
Health insurance for fellows declared medically fit
application_method: Read Annex I (Terms and Conditions) and Annex IV (List of fields of research/project titles) for the edition
Contact your National Commission for UNESCO and prepare the supporting documents
Submit the application with all supporting documents to your National Commission for UNESCO
On endorsement, e-mail the application to agh.poland@unesco.org and complete the online information sheet
official.application_route: Apply through your own National Commission for UNESCO, which selects and transmits the application to UNESCO Paris - direct applications to UNESCO are not accepted
official.citizenship_residency: Open to nationals of the 57 invited Member States listed in Annex II of the current edition only
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the fellowship is exclusively for candidates from invited developing Member States
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Individual research in the field of Science, Technology and Engineering at the UNESCO Chair for Science, Technology, and Engineering at the AGH University of Krakow; candidates must choose from the published project list in Annex III/Annex IV and some projects are restricted to particular regions
official.research_requirement: Candidates must select from the published list of proposed research projects, ranking a maximum of three by priority, and must meet the field-specific qualifications in Annex III
official.duration: 6 months of individual research; the 2025 edition ran from 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026
official.description: The Polish National Commission for UNESCO and the UNESCO Chair for Science, Technology, and Engineering at the AGH University of Krakow place 28 fellowships at the disposal of UNESCO for the benefit of developing Member States, giving beneficiaries the opportunity to undertake a six-month individual research programme in Science, Technology and Engineering.
official.english_requirement: The UNESCO fellowships application form must be completed in English using capital letters - illegible documents will be eliminated from the evaluation procedure and a handwritten form must be written in capitals only; degree certificates must be certified copies in English; a UNESCO certificate of language knowledge is required if the candidate's mother tongue is not English

not_confirmed: any deadline or edition details beyond the closed 2025 edition - no 2026 or 2027 call is published
whether the invited Member State list, project list or allowance figures change for any future edition
verification.notes: Read UNESCO's own fellowship page for the UNESCO/Poland Co-Sponsored Fellowships in Engineering, including the annex links. Amounts (PLN 1800 BSc / 2200 MSc monthly, plus the equal one-time arrival allowance), the six-month tuition-free placement at AGH Krakow, the US$120 pocket allowance and the 26 May 2025 National Commission transmission deadline are all taken from that page. The 2025 edition is closed.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a six-month engineering research fellowship at AGH University of Krakow covering free tuition, a monthly allowance of PLN 2,200 for MSc holders (PLN 1,800 for BSc), an equal one-time arrival payment, round-trip travel, health insurance and a US$120 pocket allowance - but you cannot apply to UNESCO directly. Your National Commission for UNESCO must select and transmit your application, so your first move is to contact that office in your own country months before any deadline. The 2025 edition is closed and no successor has been announced, so treat this as a watch-and-prepare opportunity rather than an open one.
applicant_utility.best_fit: BSc, MSc or PhD holders from the 57 invited Member States who can persuade their National Commission for UNESCO to nominate them for a short engineering research stay in Krakow
application_readiness_checklist: Check whether your nationality is on the current edition's Annex II list of invited Member States - the list is re-issued every edition and has changed between editions
Contact your National Commission for UNESCO early to learn its internal national deadline, which will be earlier than UNESCO's own
Rank a maximum of three projects from the published list, and check Annex III and Annex IV in case your region is excluded from your preferred project
Get your degree certificates apostilled or legalised and translated into English now - this is the step that most often runs out of time
Line up two referees who know your work well enough to write dated recommendation letters for that specific edition
common_rejection_risks: Sending an application straight to UNESCO - individual applications are not accepted, only those endorsed by a National Commission
Missing your National Commission's internal cut-off, which sits well before UNESCO's transmission deadline
Submitting an incomplete file - candidatures with missing documents are discarded outright
Writing the four-page form in mixed case or illegibly; the rules explicitly eliminate illegible documents and require capitals on handwritten forms
Choosing a project for which only candidates from another region are eligible
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Passport and visa expenses, which UNESCO and the Government of Poland explicitly do not fund, and any personal spending beyond the monthly allowance and US$120 pocket money
document_audit: All four pages of the UNESCO application form must be completed - a partly filled form is treated as incomplete
Degrees must be certified copies in English with Apostille, or legalised in the country of issue if Apostille is not recognised; a plain photocopy is not enough
The two recommendation letters must be dated within the edition's own year - letters from an earlier cycle do not count
You must supply an identity photo copy as well as a passport copy, and a UNESCO certificate of language knowledge if your mother tongue is not English
alerts: The route through your National Commission is the entire application - there is no direct channel and no appeal if the Commission does not nominate you
The 2025 edition is closed with no successor announced, so verify a live call before preparing documents
The stipend differs by degree level (PLN 1,800 BSc vs PLN 2,200 MSc) and by edition, so confirm both against the current annexes rather than assuming last cycle's figures
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Contact your National Commission for UNESCO, prepare the four-page form and certified documents nationally, wait for endorsement, then e-mail the endorsed application to agh.poland@unesco.org and complete the online information sheet before the deadline
